intended_object: The directional (line) derivative of f at x in direction v: the limit of (f(x+tv) − f(x))/t as t → 0, i.e. the derivative at 0 of t ↦ f(x + t v), with value 0 if it does not exist (from docstring and name).
explanation: The body is deriv (fun t ↦ f (x + t • v)) 0, which is exactly the directional derivative of f at x along v. When that derivative doesn't exist, deriv returns 0, matching the docstring's "zero otherwise". This is the usual junk-value convention. The generality is natural. E only needs to be a 𝕜-module, with no topology, since only the line t ↦ x + t•v is used. F is a normed space over any nontrivially normed field, which is the setting deriv requires. This is the Mathlib declaration itself, and Mathlib has no more general version of it.
